A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original multimodal registration and few-shot segmentation results, controlled ablations, sensitivity analyses, and negative results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, with additional ultrasound and microscopy segmentation experiments and DINOv2 and SuPreM comparisons in Appendices A.6-A.8.

M1.justification: The synthetic label and appearance generators, multiscale contrastive objective, UNet architecture, and downstream procedures are unchanged. Revised explanations and augmentation disclosures do not establish a procedural change; LoRA/FPN adaptation concerns the new DINOv2 baseline.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 expands evaluation beyond CT/MRI to SegThy neck ultrasound and NucMM-M microscopy of mouse cortical nuclei. These introduce different acquisition modalities, anatomy, biological scale, and population. NucMM-M is evaluated as binary semantic segmentation, not instance segmentation.

E2.justification: Appendices A.7-A.8 add two distinct comparator strategies: slice-wise DINOv2 with LoRA and an FPN decoder on all six main segmentation datasets, and AbdomenAtlas-pretrained SuPreM on the five MRI datasets. Existing comparisons retain their baseline membership.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce SegThy splits of 2/4/6 training/validation/testing subjects, NucMM-M splits of 1/3/4 volumes, ultrasound resampling, and microscopy label binarization. DINOv2 introduces slice-wise 2D adaptation with LoRA/FPN and validation-based checkpoint selection. These substantially extend the evaluation design; previously reported splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 newly reports qualitative comparisons favoring full finetuning over linear probing and longer training with gradual learning-rate decay, without numerical breakdowns. Existing label-source, temperature, loss, augmentation, network-size, annotation-budget, and registration-sensitivity analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrapped standard deviations for segmentation results and configuration spread for registration grid searches. New Tables 7-9 follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1-6 and figure results are unchanged, but Tables 7-9 add substantial results. Ours achieves mean Dice 0.84 on SegThy and 0.89 on NucMM-M, behind SMIT's 0.91 on the latter. New WUFetal scores are 0.43 for DINOv2 and 0.71 for SuPreM, versus the retained 0.76 for Ours. These are additional comparisons, not improved scores for the proposed method between versions.

T1.justification: The contrastive-loss definition, registration objectives, mathematical assumptions, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Neither version adds formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Several introduction and conclusion statements qualify the scope as radiological tasks or contexts, where v1 used broader biomedical or unrestricted task wording. The central contributions—synthetic data generation and general-purpose representations for registration and segmentation—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 extends the intensity-invariance limitation to texture-dependent tasks. Appendices A.7-A.8 interpret the new comparisons as supporting native 3D representations and broader transfer than abdominal-CT pretraining, and speculate about combining synthetic and real training data. Existing mechanism explanations and negative-result interpretations remain.

D1.justification: New implementation disclosures identify the DINOv2 ViT-L/14 encoder with registers, LoRA/FPN adaptation, channel replication, and added dataset preparation. Existing sections now specify MRI sequences and clarify augmentation defaults and SynthMorph's lack of test-time tuning. The proposed model's implementation and code/weights access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for DINOv2 medical adaptations, LoRA, SuPreM/AbdomenAtlas, the new datasets, and texture-dependent applications. The introduction replaces its chest-X-ray example with abdominal-CT foundation models. These extend the existing positioning without substantially reorganizing the related-work argument.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose corrections, clarifies data-engine explanations, adds radiology qualifiers and Appendices A.6-A.8, and changes the header from preprint to ICLR 2025 publication. The main section order and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three result tables and revises several figure captions and the dataset-modality row. All twelve existing figure images are retained. Original implementation Tables 7-9 become Tables 10-12, with modest page reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V1 supported broad biomedical generalization through CT/MRI experiments. V2 addresses an important coverage gap with ultrasound and microscopy, while testing competing approaches based on general 2D pretraining and large-scale real CT pretraining. These additions substantially strengthen evidence for the central generalization claim while preserving existing ablations and negative results. The small added test sets and specific baseline adaptations still limit broader conclusions.
